headline: Answering critics at Grant's Tomb
summary: In Newark, Roosevelt speaks as a new statue of Lincoln is unveiled. At Grant's Tomb that Decoration Day, he criticizes Taft's policies and answers wealthy critics who claim his ideas invite revolution, saying true revolutionaries fear him most.

events.detail: Speaks at a Lincoln statue unveiling
Decoration Day address at Grant's Tomb criticizing Taft

tr_quotes.text: If they will read the utterances of men who really do desire revolution, they will see that those men hate me, and dread me more than those men who call themselves conservative.

headline: Tutoring Archie for Harvard
summary: Roosevelt tells Oscar King Davis he has no intention of running in 1912 and notes Stimson's appointment as Secretary of War. He writes Lodge about the arbitration treaty and Lodge's Outlook article on American folk myths. Archie is home studying for Harvard exams, with Edith teaching him French and his father history and civics.
